extracted.intended_audience: Reuters journalists, correspondents, editors and copy-editors
extracted.subtask_description: A newsroom style guide for writing and editing news copy to Reuters standards, covering impartiality, sourcing, punctuation, spelling, capitalization, numbers, conversions and sensitive-word usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality vs colour in descriptive reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance the need for impartiality and concise writing with the need for colour, description and atmosphere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correspondents filing witness reports should think visual and write copy that reflects being on the scene rather than second-hand; if writing from the office, descriptive material may be taken from television but distinguish clearly between what television shows (facts need not be sourced if indisputable) and what a television commentator says. Vivid quotes and lively background details should be woven into copy, not inserted in slabs. Avoid gaudy adjectives and overdramatic verbs; choose the right noun and use vigorous, active verbs. First person should not normally intrude; if sourcing a contentious statement based on direct observation, write 'This correspondent saw…'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'coloured' (race term)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'coloured' for people only in the context of South Africa for a person of mixed race.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the context clear. Lower case. See section on race.

rubrics_metrics.name: American verb form 'combated'
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'combated' as the American usage for the verb 'combat'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'comedian'
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'comedian' for a man or a woman.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use 'comedienne'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenation of U.S. titles
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no hyphens in U.S. titles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g. 'commander in chief' (American style) rather than 'commander-in-chief'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plural of 'commando'
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'commandos' as the plural.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comma usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use commas to clarify sense but avoid overuse; rewrite sentences with too many commas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use commas to mark apposition (e.g. Herve de Charette, French foreign minister, said ...), to mark non-essential clauses (The airliner, which was seven years old, crashed ...) but not essential clauses (The airliner that crashed on Thursday was seven years old). Use commas to separate list items; normally no comma before the final 'and' unless omission risks ambiguity. A comma follows an initial 'however'; opening phrases like 'On Wednesday the committee decided ...' need not be followed by a comma unless ambiguous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer 'begin' or 'start' to 'commence'
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'begin' or 'start' instead of 'commence'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalists should not 'comment'
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should not comment; they should interpret events by reporting the action of others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial paper definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Short-term debt issued by companies for working capital, typically with about 90 days duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verb and noun forms: 'commit' and 'commitment'
rubrics_metrics.description: Past tense is 'committed'; noun is 'commitment'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'official communique' tautology
rubrics_metrics.description: A communique is an official announcement; 'official communique' is tautological.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer 'plain statement' in many cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lower-case 'communist' unless party name
rubrics_metrics.description: Use lower case 'communist' except when referring to a specific party (e.g. Communist Party of Great Britain).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'Comoros' for Comoro Islands
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'the Comoros' for the Indian Ocean group; 'Comoro Islands' alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Company names at first reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the full legal company name (including Inc, Ltd, Plc etc.) at first reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If clumsy (several companies in a lead), the full legal name can be given at second reference. Give the name in its original language if Latin characters are used unless the company prefers an English name. Observe company spelling, capitalization and punctuation (apostrophes, hyphens, slashes), but use standard abbreviations for company type without a full stop (Inc not Inc.). If a company styles its name all in capitals, render it upper/lower (CIGNA Corp becomes Cigna Corp). Eliminate exclamation points in company names (e.g. Yahoo! becomes Yahoo). Keep lower case in company names except at the start of a sentence (eBay becomes Ebay). Do not pluralise company names or the pronouns referring to them; companies are singular.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of company-type abbreviations
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard abbreviations that indicate the kind of registered company (AB, AG, A/S, Cie, Co, Cos, Corp, GmbH, Inc, KK, Ltd, Plc, Pty, SpA, YK).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When such abbreviations come at the end of a company name they are not preceded by a comma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate title capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize corporate titles when used formally before a name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g. Company Chairman John Smith, not Company chairman John Smith.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'compare with' vs 'compare to'
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'compare with' to highlight differences or similarities; 'compare to' is used when simply stating that two things are similar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g. His playing compares to that of Mozart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make like-with-like comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare like with like; avoid mismatched comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not compare a shortage with years or a distance with a weapon. Be careful with statistical comparisons across months or countries with non-comparable attributes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'comparatively' only when actually comparing
rubrics_metrics.description: Only use 'comparatively' if comparing something with another; often it can be omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compass points capitalization and hyphenation
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize compass points only when part of a proper name (North Korea) but lower case when general (north London). Omit hyphens in the four basic compounds northwest, northeast, southwest, southeast; use hyphen in minor compounds like north-northeast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use 'northern Chiang Mai' when meaning 'the northern town of Chiang Mai'; similar for provinces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer 'expatriate' not 'expatriot'
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'expatriate' as correct spelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish 'complacent' and 'complaisant'
rubrics_metrics.description: Complacent = smug/self-satisfied; complaisant = willing and affable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complement vs compliment
rubrics_metrics.description: To complement is to complete or match; to compliment is to praise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use examples to avoid confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'comprise' only for whole listing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'comprise' only when listing all the component parts of a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not write 'comprised of'; when listing only some components use 'include'. E.g. 'Benelux comprises Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenate compound adjectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Compound adjectives require hyphens (e.g. 'first-leg score').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an adverb and adjective are used in an adjectival phrase, no hyphen is used (e.g. 'a closely followed competition').

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer 'about' to 'concerning'
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'about' rather than 'concerning'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid vague 'confrontation'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Confrontation' is modish but vague; use specific terms like war, clash, dispute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congo naming
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and the neighbouring Congo Republic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In most stories, only one Congo involved so subsequent references can be 'Congo' or 'Congolese'. Use 'DRC' in bracket at first mention for Democratic Republic of Congo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalize 'Congress' but lower-case 'congressional'
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize 'Congress' when part of the name of an official body; keep 'congressional' lower case unless part of a formal title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'connote' and 'denote' when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions: denoted = indicate; connote = imply attributes, but both are probably best avoided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenation for '-conscious' words
rubrics_metrics.description: Hyphenate as in 'self-conscious' but 'unconsciousness' (no hyphen).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid tautology 'general consensus'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Consensus' already means unanimity or a general trend of opinion; phrases like 'general consensus' are tautological.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'because' rather than 'as a consequence of'
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer concise phrasing: use 'because' rather than the verbose 'as a consequence of'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lower-case 'conservative' unless party name
rubrics_metrics.description: Use lower case 'conservative' unless referring to a specific political organisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'considerable' — define by size
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid vague adjectives like 'considerable'; define by size and show the reader why something is considerable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plural of 'consortium'
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'consortiums', not 'consortia'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenate 'consul-general'
rubrics_metrics.description: Use hyphen in 'consul-general' and 'consulate-general'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'consult' not 'consult with'
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer the shorter 'consult' rather than 'consult with'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer Price Index (CPI) usage
rubrics_metrics.description: CPI = a measure of retail price inflation, usually given as percent rise or fall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also known as retail price index; in the UK, main domestic measure equal to HICP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spelling corrections (contagious, contango etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use correct spellings: 'contagious' not 'contageous'; 'contango' definition provided for futures context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference: contemptible vs contemptuous
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Contemptible' = despicable; 'contemptuous' = haughty or scornful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'continue' in leads
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid 'continue' in lead paragraphs; choose more lively phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continual vs continuous
rubrics_metrics.description: Continual = frequent and repeated; continuous = uninterrupted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid contractions in narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid contractions (isn't, won't) except in direct quotations; spell out in full in copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'contrast to' vs 'contrast with'
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'contrast to' for comparisons of dissimilar things; use 'contrast with' to compare differences of two similar things.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 'compare' guidance for nuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'controversial' — spell it out
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid the vague word 'controversial'; spell out what is controversial and let the reader decide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversions: currencies and units
rubrics_metrics.description: Convert currencies into U.S. dollars and convert imperial weights and measures into metric equivalents and vice versa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give the local unit first, then conversion in brackets. Never give the dollar equivalent without the local currency first. If original figure approximate, conversion should be approximate. Write 'a 2,000-lb (900-kg) bomb' not '2,000-lb (907-kg)'. Do not give more decimal places than original. Use singular metric abbreviations without a full stop (kg, km). If no specific figure is given, do not convert. Double-check conversions and do a rough backward check after calculator use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversions in sports writing
rubrics_metrics.description: In sports writing use only metric measurements except golf (yards/feet) and sailing (nautical miles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No need to add conversions in brackets apart from currencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'conveyor' for belt and person
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'conveyor' for conveyor belt and for a person who conveys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convince vs persuade
rubrics_metrics.description: You 'convince' someone of something and 'persuade' them to do something.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenation exceptions for 'co-' words
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Cooperate' and 'coordination' are exceptions to hyphenation rules (no hyphen).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'co-op' for the store sense to distinguish from 'coop'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'helicopter' not 'copter'
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer the full word 'helicopter'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-respondent vs correspondent
rubrics_metrics.description: A co-respondent appears in a divorce case; a correspondent writes letters (or is a reporter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization: 'Corporate America' not 'corporate America'
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'corporate America' (lower case 'corporate').

rubrics_metrics.name: Spelling: 'council' and 'councillor' vs US 'counsel'
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'council' and 'councillor'; American style uses 'counsel', 'counseling', 'counselor'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court of St. James's spelling
rubrics_metrics.description: The place to which ambassadors are posted in Great Britain is 'Court of St. James’s' (St. not St and James’s not James Palace).

rubrics_metrics.name: Court-martial pluralisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'court-martial' and plural 'courts-martial'; verb 'to court-martial'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use courtesy titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use courtesy titles (Mr, Mrs, Ms, Miss) or foreign equivalents in copy generally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: in a story about two people with same family name (Mr Smith and Mrs Smith) to avoid confusion. Use at first reference only titles of nobility and military, medical and religious titles (Lord Ferrars, Dr Christiaan Barnard). Avoid foreign honorifics except obvious cases (king/queen). Prefer job title or position to honorifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover up (verb) vs coverup (noun)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use two words for the verb ('cover up') and one word for the noun ('coverup').

rubrics_metrics.name: Use exact credit rating notation and spell out plus/minus
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the exact combination of letters and case the rating agencies use; spell out '+' or '-' as 'plus' or 'minus'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Standard & Poor's AAA, AA-plus, AA-minus; Moody's Aaa, Aa1, Aa3; Fitch AAA, AA-plus, AA-minus. See agency websites for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid wrong use of 'crescendo'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Crescendo' is a gradual increase in loudness; saying something 'reached a crescendo' is incorrect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer 'climax' if that is intended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease abbreviation
rubrics_metrics.description: Can be abbreviated to CJD (explain on first use). Variant vCJD also used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abbreviate to vCJD for variant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'cripple' to describe disabled people
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid using 'cripple' to describe the handicapped; be sensitive in referring to disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mention disabilities only if relevant and avoid sentimentality or condescension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'crisis' sparingly and accurately
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Crisis' means a turning point and is often overused; avoid the term unless it's accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A crisis cannot 'grow' or 'deepen'; it just is.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spelling 'crisscross' as one word
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Crisscross' is one word.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plural of 'curriculum vitae'
rubrics_metrics.description: Singular 'curriculum vitae'; plural 'curricula vitae'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'cut' for 'cutback' both verb and noun
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'cut' rather than 'cutback' for both verb and noun senses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verb vs noun: 'cut off' / 'cutoff'
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'cut off' (two words) for the verb and 'cutoff' (one word) for the noun.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'tsar' not 'czar'
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer 'tsar' spelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer 'Krakow' for Cracow
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'Krakow, Poland' spelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give source for controversial crowd estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: If the number of people at an event is controversial, give the source for the number quoted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'crucial' cliché
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid overused adjective 'crucial'; show why something is crucial and to whom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lower-case 'cruise missile'
rubrics_metrics.description: Use lower case for 'cruise missile'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spellings and word-choice corrections (wide range)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple single-word entries specify preferred spellings and correct usages (e.g. 'contagious' not 'contageous', 'doughnut' not 'donut' unless company name, 'dike' not 'dyke', 'die-hard' hyphenated, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the provided examples and replacements in each entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dates formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Use month/day/year sequence (Iraq’s invasion of Kuwait on Aug. 2, 1990) or spell out month in text; in datelines abbreviate months without full stop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When spelling out duration, write 'May 22 to 24' not 'May 22-24'; write 'arrived on Monday' not 'arrived Monday' (exception for Americas). Use '1939-45 war' but 'from 1939 to 1945' not 'from 1939-45'. Write '9/11' not '9-11'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data treated as singular in practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Strictly plural noun, but treat 'data' as if singular in Reuters usage (e.g. 'The data was corrupted').

rubrics_metrics.name: Dashes vs hyphens
rubrics_metrics.description: Use dashes sparingly; dashes should be double (–) and hyphens single (-).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Never use dashes to set off relative clauses in a sentence; a single dash may be used as a separator in alerts and headlines where space is tight, but not in text. Dashes are followed by lower case unless used to label list sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbers and decades
rubrics_metrics.description: Write '1960s' not '1960’s'; spell out 'the early forties, sixties, seventies.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Deletion/ellipsis in quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate omitted words from a quote by three full stops with a space before and after (ellipsis): 'We will fight ... and we will win.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The word after the dots is capitalised if it begins a new sentence. Drop words only if deletion does not alter the sense of the quote.
